---
title: "HB Realization and Case Outcomes"
subtitle: "How are modes normalized and partial batches kept consumable?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design.

## Materialize one request-global mode lattice

Python validates pump axes, drive identities, case currents, truncation, and
trace modes. Julia materializes the finite ordered Fourier lattice once for the
request, records signed physical frequencies, and lowers each case's effective
source coefficients to JosephsonCircuits indices.

SCNSim uses `exp(-i omega t)`, while JosephsonCircuits uses the opposite phasor
convention. Source coefficients therefore follow the exact conjugate-mode map
in the Runtime Contract. Response adaptation first reorders by the same signed
physical frequency, then conjugates once and applies the input/output frequency
normalization. Zero-frequency response modes and ambiguous frequency collisions
fail before numerical response construction.

## Derive the same selected network

For each case, Julia normalizes full mode-by-Port `returnZ`, de-embeds backend
source resistors, applies PTC, pair transforms, retained mapping, omitted
matched loads, and selected reference boundaries in the contract order. Public
Y, Z, and matrix-reference power-wave S all come from that one selected
network. Native S is retained only as reconciliation evidence.

Reconciliation lifts the Port map to the canonical port-major/mode-minor basis.
A plain original-Port subset is comparable when omitted channels keep matched
loads; unequal PTC, topology, reference, frequency, or normalization produces
typed non-comparability rather than a fabricated residual.

## Seal one outcome for every case

Case numerical work is isolated within the batch process. Every declared case
produces an `HBCaseOutcome` in declaration order. Success contains S/Y/Z,
traces, source states, and evidence, with `failure is None`. Numerical failure
sets `failure` to a receipt-reconstructible `HBCaseFailure` carrying a stable
kind, stage, message, and available case evidence. Accessing a success-only
property raises that same typed failure.

The final batch may be fully successful, partial, or all-numerical-failure and
is still a completed, reusable typed request result. Case failures do not make
the request retryable. A runtime, protocol, or receipt-integrity failure fails
the request itself and may be retried as a new attempt. `hb.show()` plots
successes and visibly lists all failures. Direct and HB retain their own
requested grids; presentation does not interpolate them.
